content: A reference range is a collection of values that healthcare professionals use to interpret the results of medical tests. This range is typically defined as the span of values within which 95% of the normal population falls. The reference range can vary depending on factors such as the age, sex, and race of the population being tested. Additionally, the specific instruments and methodologies used by the laboratory to conduct the tests can also influence the reference range. It is important to note that, by definition, 5% of the normal population will have test results that fall outside of the established reference range, even in the absence of any underlying medical condition.
